summary: Douglas County Coast Range lookout: a 1913 log cabin, a wooden tower from the 1930s, burned in the 1951 Hubbard Creek fire and not rebuilt.

facts.status_note: The wooden tower burned in the 1951 Hubbard Creek fire; the register lists the site as gone.

events.note: 14 x 20 log cabin built on the summit after the fire season, at a cost of $125
Register date for a 40-foot wooden live-in tower replacing the cabin; a 1935 item gives 50 feet

Ida Beeman spent the summer at Landers; another lookout transferred there
Newspaper reports dated August 21, 1951 say the tower and structure beneath it burned in the path of the Hubbard Creek fire; the News-Review report dated August 22 says the burning tower fell
A 1951 state allocation for rebuilding was reported in June 1952 as not going ahead: the lookout will not be reconstructed

notes_for_editor: Register (1933, 40 ft) and the 1935 newspaper item (50 ft, completed 1935) disagree on date and height. The record's height_m 15.2 matches the 50-foot figure, not the register; left unchanged. The Douglas County plan does not name Landers, so the link to Landers rests on the 1951 newspaper item. The plan's Hubbard Creek Fire (1951, 15,574 acres) fits the newspaper account of a Hubbard Creek fire 20 miles north of Roseburg; a Hubbard Creek fire near Detroit in the federal lessons database may be a different fire. The story now says the newspapers date the burning to August 21 and the fall to August 22, and does not treat the plan as naming Landers. No source describes the site, its remains or its access today; record access 'unknown' left as is. Staffing 'seasonal' inferred from fire-season wording and the last dated staffing (1949).
